verdict: The plan's shared preparation works as one step on all six backends that ship, as long as the three backend-only steps stay (SCIP tiny terms, CPLEX same point, GLPK stall). I wrote it as one function, fp::prepare in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-plaiseek-Projects-mippp/b99a8387-c5e9-4bc6-9141-d4502a992e5d/scratchpad/user_cuts/final_prepare.hpp, and used it in place of each recipe's sanitize. The conformance set passes at the skeptics' sizes: Gurobi 12.0.1 72/72, CPLEX 22.1.2 64/64, Xpress 47.01.01 R1 49/49, COPT 8.0.5 49/49 at DELAY 0 and 49/49 at DELAY 20, SCIP 9.2.1 49/49 plain and 49/49 deep, GLPK 5.0 49/49. These match verify_results.json case for case. The scale sweep is right in 360 of 360 runs against Gurobi's MIPGap-0 optimum. The no-scaling control has power: 19 wrong, failed or aborted runs (COPT 5, SCIP 1, GLPK 13) and none on Gurobi, CPLEX or Xpress. Scaling does not hurt the three backends that did not need it. CPLEX, Xpress and COPT explore exactly the same number of nodes with and without it. Gurobi is never worse, and is much better with 1e12 cuts, which it otherwise ignores. Two changes to the plan's order: split == before the drop, and reject non-finite input first. The SCIP tiny-term step is more than a refinement: the shared scaling itself creates the SCIP fault (12/12 wrong without the step, 12/12 right unscaled), and the step's cost is that cuts whose coefficients span 1e9 or more become useless on SCIP. Natural separators never produced a cut violated by between 1e-9 and 1e-6, and conformance passes at 1e-9 everywhere. The 1e-6 drop matters only on GLPK, in one case: the GLPK skeptic's conditional big-M cut (cover − K x_b). The drop removes that family from K = 1e6 on every backend, not only GLPK. On GLPK both alternatives fail: unscaled K = 1e10 gives a value above the true maximum, reported optimal; the 1e-9 drop stalls to the time limit. No scaling choice fixes COPT 8.0.5 with presolve off: valid cuts with a 1e9–1e10 coefficient range give false optima (7/10 with the plan's scaling), while all runs at COPT's default presolve were right. D4 also reproduces on CPLEX, where the callback never runs. It does not reproduce on COPT. On Xpress the callback does run, but D1 makes every arm report infeasible, so the value tells nothing.

Nearly every number I traced matches survey_results.json, verify_results.json or a raw output: 106.4 of 107.4, 1718 for 1733, 10 to 13 of 40, 314842200 reads, 16.9 s for 8 s, 1.60 over 46 pairs, 6997 to 1, 58 of 58 and 4365 runs, 40 of 40 against 22 of 40, and 14 of 33. All cited repo lines say what the plan says: model_concepts.hpp:826-834, model_base.hpp:299-301, 314 and 340-354, copt_milp.hpp:95-98 and 124, xpress_milp.hpp:100, gurobi_milp.hpp:230-233, cplex_milp.hpp:115-118, 131, 147, 182 and 232-244, glpk_milp.hpp:103-110 and 345-348, cbc_milp.hpp:726 and 736, cbc_api.hpp:99-105, scip_milp.hpp:100-110, and the docs lines. Every vendor quote I pulled is verbatim: Xpress 'might be used on any node' and preintsol note 4, the MUTEXCALLBACKS routine list, CPLEX 'the rest of the model', the SCIP FAQ, var.c:14312, sepastore.c:459, the MOSEK prohibition, and COPT 11090/11259/5719. Rerunning own_xpress_reject reproduced D1 exactly. copt_cmd at Threads=1 reproduced the COPT false optimum (11996.999999906 at 0.0000% gap; 12135 at default threads, with Presolve=0, and on Gurobi). The problems are of four kinds. Some statements are wrong: Gurobi also needs LazyConstraints=1 for a lazy row from MIPNODE; SCIP maxrounds=0 leaves 6 root calls; the Xpress equality crash is inside XPRSaddmanagedcuts on the recommended path; GLPK's 'presolve-solved' silent case has no source; 'every fault below is silent' contradicts the aborts in the same table; COPT's guide does promise a call on every solved LP; and D4 is described by a mechanism my rerun did not show (calls=1, lazy_added=1, answer still 5). Some refined claims are repeated in their unrefined form: incumbents 'not bound', Gurobi 'one call per node', COPT 'lost except where absent', Cbc 'local'. Some one-instance numbers are stated as rules: Cbc 99.6%, CPLEX 200x, PreCrush 100 to 300x, COPT 58691. Finally, omissions bear on Decisions 4 and 5: COPT's serialization is no more promised than Xpress's, and a shared 1e-6 drop after scaling would drop big-M cuts on every backend, not only on GLPK (that last point is my inference).

findings.where: Decisions for the maintainer (none covers it); Proposed interface comment 'c must hold at every integer feasible point of the model'
findings.what: The deletion filter's trials go through solve(), so a relaxation callback attached per solve runs a separator in every trial. A trial relaxes rows and bounds. A cut valid for the full model, for example a cover cut derived from row R, cuts off feasible points of a trial that relaxed R. That trial then reads infeasible, the filter drops R, and it reports `irreducible` for a set that is feasible. The contract cannot protect the trials: the filter runs only on infeasible models, where 'valid at every integer feasible point' is vacuous and every cut qualifies. Lazy constraints can be background because they define the model (deletion-filter.md:183). User cuts by design never carry feasibility (plan:64-66), so they cannot be.
findings.evidence: final_iis_usercuts.cpp, Gurobi 12.0.1. A native MIPNODE callback stands in for the proposed one: it stays registered because gurobi_milp::_attached_callbacks attaches nothing when no MIP++ callback is set (gurobi_milp.hpp:220-226). Model: x in {0,1}^6, y in [0.5,2], M: 2 sum x + y == 6.5, R: 2 sum x <= 5. The cut is sum x <= 2, offered when violated. final_iis_usercuts.txt: 'seed  0 control  : irreducible M=true R=true y<=2:true y>=0.5:false x-bounds=0' against 'seed  0 separator: irreducible M=true R=false y<=2:true y>=0.5:true x-bounds=6 | separator calls=3 cuts=3 | trials I*I*I*FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF'. Seeds 0 to 19 gave the identical path, so this is one deterministic reproduction, not 20 independent trials. The returned set (M, both y sides, x bounds, no R) is feasible by arithmetic: sum x = 3 with y = 0.5. docs/algorithms/deletion-filter.md:103: 'A trial is a solve(), so a registered candidate-solution callback runs in every trial, and its lazy constraints and rejections are background too'.
findings.replacement: Add a decision 8. 'Deletion filter. (a) Recommended: compute_iis_by_deletion runs its trials without the node-relaxation callback, through a detail-level suspension the engine takes when has_node_relaxation_callback<M>. Cost: one internal hook per backend, since the engine is generic and has no public way to suspend and restore one callback. (b) Cheaper fallback: document, as deletion-filter.md:185 does for callbacks with memory, that with a node-relaxation callback set an irreducible answer is unproven, and tell users to clear it first.' verdict: I took the plan's facts as given. It still leaves out things that would change five of its seven decisions. (1) The probe I ran found a shipped wrong-answer defect the defect table does not list. On CPLEX 22.1.2 and COPT 8.0.5, `add_lazy_constraint` rejects the candidate even when the candidate satisfies the constraint, so the optimum is lost at `status::optimal` (6 for 7). Gurobi 12.0.1 accepts the same candidate. D3's empty-lazy case on COPT is one instance of this. The plan's own drop-satisfied step is the fix, so it has to serve the lazy path too. (2) The Xpress gate at 45.01.04 cannot be written under the current version rules. Xpress validated starts at 45.1, the shared wrapper FAILs `feature_unavailable_error` on a validated release, and the skill requires any floor to sit at or below every validated bound. (3) The mutex is per lambda. CPLEX runs CANDIDATE and RELAXATION at the same time, so a separator shared between lazy constraints and user cuts still races. COPT is serialized with no vendor promise, the same as Xpress, yet the plan gives it no mutex. (4) `compute_iis_by_deletion` runs every registered callback in each trial. A cut that is valid for the full model can be invalid in a trial where a row or bound was relaxed, which can corrupt the IIS. (5) Two of the five first-wave backends, SCIP and Xpress, have no correct lazy path today. The plan's own rule, lazy constraints for feasibility, and its DFJ example therefore cannot be followed there. On local cuts, "not now" stands, but its reason is wrong where it matters. An indicator is a model-level constraint and cannot be added from a hook. The big-M rewrite works only for subtrees defined by binary fixings, and it needs the node's bounds, which Gurobi and COPT, the two solvers without a local flag, cannot read. The plan also never says what a user with local cuts can do on each backend. The cut-preparation table is missing a non-finite check, which GLPK aborts on. The GLPK section is missing the empty-model case, which aborts the process. CPLEX's moving root loop at a violation of 1e-5 is not covered by either guard. Decision 5 applies max-scaling on Gurobi, CPLEX and Xpress, where I found no run that sent scaled cuts. Cuts derived from an incumbent or a cutoff, integer-free models, error handling inside the handle, tests and docs are not addressed.

That form works only when the subtree is defined by binary fixings: a general-integer branching bound has no linear global form without a new variable. It needs a finite M_j for every variable in the cut. It needs the node's bounds, which Gurobi and COPT cannot read, and those are exactly the two solvers without a local flag. It also grows by one term per fixing, is nearly redundant outside the subtree, and its big M runs into the plan's own scaling and 1e-6 drop. Where it can be written it is safe: Gurobi held big-M cuts. The plan also never says what a user with genuinely local cuts can do on each backend. The native route is closed on three backends, because solve() takes or clears the slot.
